pantograph: The tram's roof pantograph: a red folding diamond of steel arms with springs, its carbon contact strip pressing up on the single overhead copper wire, mounted on insulators on the roof, roof equipment boxes around its base.
wire: The single overhead contact wire of the tram line hanging from thin cross-wires on slim steel poles, above the tram roof, with the pale river and town houses behind.
roof: The tram's roof cut open: grey boxes of traction inverters with cooling grilles, air-conditioning units, braking resistors, orange high-voltage cables, the black accordion joint between sections.
cab: The tram's front driver's cab behind the curved windscreen: the driver in a light blue shirt at his desk with screens and a single speed-control handle, the windscreen wiper, the red-and-white front.
front-bogie: The front motor bogie under the tram's nose: two big steel wheels on the rails, a round grey electric traction motor and gearbox between them, yellow and orange pipes, springs and the frame.
saloon: The inside of the tram's first section: passengers sitting on red seats and standing holding yellow poles and straps, a parent with a pushchair in the open space, windows and an information screen.
doors: Wide open sliding double doors of the low-floor tram with passengers stepping in and out at the level of the stop, yellow grab poles, the black accordion joint next to them.
joint: The tram's articulation joints: black accordion-folded bellows between the white-and-red body sections, with the round turntable floor plate and the bogie under the joint.
bogie: The tram's middle bogies: small steel wheels on the grooved rails, disc brakes, a magnetic track brake shoe hanging just above the rail, springs and the frame under the body.
rails: Two pairs of shiny steel grooved tram rails set flush into the grey and beige cobbled street, the narrow groove visible in the rail head, the tram's wheels running on them at the top.
points: Tram switch points in the cobbled street: the rails splitting into two tracks, two thin moving steel switch blades, and the small grey switch motor box and cover plates set into the cobbles.
stop: The tram stop: a slim glass and steel shelter with a bench, people waiting with bags, a red ticket machine with a screen, the stop pole, and the raised platform kerb.
